dish: Italian beef, dipped, with hot giardiniera or sweet peppers
w: The Taylor Street original (1938) where the family claims the Italian beef was invented; the beef for every Al's is still roasted here. #1 on the Infatuation's Italian-beef ranking and a fixture of every Chicago beef list.

dish: Italian beef with hot peppers, char-grilled Italian sausage, lemon Italian ice
address: 7500 W North Ave, Elmwood Park, IL 60707
w: Elmwood Park walk-up open since 1961 — Steve Dolinsky's (ABC7 Hungry Hound) #1 Italian beef in the suburbs, with an 'ambrosial' jus, and the lemon ice that closes every order.

dish: Pan pizza with the caramelized-cheese crust
w: Lincoln Park's pan-pizza bar whose pies are ringed with blackened, caramelized cheese — the deep dish many Chicagoans name first (Infatuation) and #8 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking.

dish: Deep dish on the buttercrust; the 'Lou' (spinach, mushroom, three cheeses, tomato)
w: The family that helped invent deep dish (Lou worked at Uno before opening his own in 1971); Infatuation calls it the best version of the classic Chicago pie — sauce on top, flaky buttery crust.

dish: Sourdough deep dish on a 48-hour cold-fermented, cornmeal-crisp crust
w: Edgewater carryout doing a focaccia-like sourdough deep dish; on both the Infatuation deep-dish ranking and Time Out's top pizza list.

dish: Pan pizza with a caramelized crust
w: Pandemic-born Uptown pan-pizza shop in the Pequod's lineage — #2 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking and on the Infatuation deep-dish list.

dish: Tavern-style thin crust, party (square) cut, with sausage
w: Ashburn's tavern-pizza shrine since the 1940s — #1 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking ('the king of tavern-style') and the spot with the most 'best' nods in Chowhound's tavern-pizza research.

dish: Paper-thin tavern crust with house-made smoky sausage
w: Family-run Lincoln Park pizzeria (since 1950) whose flaky, cracker-thin crust is on Time Out's top-pizza ranking and Chowhound's best tavern-style list.

dish: Tavern-style pies on a six-day fermented sourdough crust
w: Tiny West Town pizzeria in a former barbershop from veteran Chicago pizza makers — #3 on Time Out's citywide ranking, #1 on Chowhound's tavern list and an Esquire Best New Restaurant 2025.

dish: Old-school tavern-style pizza with house beer and regional produce
w: Logan Square brewpub-bakery; on Time Out's top-pizza ranking and the only brewpub on Chowhound's tavern-pizza list.

dish: The Superdawg in its box with a pickled green tomato; Whoopskidawg
w: The 1948 carhop drive-in under the two giant hot-dog mascots on the roof — on both the Infatuation and Time Out best-hot-dog lists.

dish: The Depression dog (mustard, onion, relish, sport peppers) buried in fresh-cut fries — no ketchup
address: 2720 N River Rd, River Grove, IL 60171
w: River Grove stand (1946; here since 1950) — no seats, no ketchup; the gold standard of the Depression dog on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.

dish: Chicago-style char dog; Vienna char-grilled Polish
w: West Ridge stand famous since 1967 for its sign — a giant hot dog on a fork — and a char dog both the Infatuation and Time Out rank among the city's best.

dish: Depression dog with fries; fries with cheese sauce
w: Cheap, late Depression-dog stand on Armitage — on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.

dish: Vienna Beef Chicago-style dog with everything
address: 1017 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60613
w: Classic Wrigleyville hot-dog stand serving the North Side since 1975 — reviewed by the Infatuation and on Time Out's best-hot-dogs list.

dish: The Mother-in-Law (tamale in a hot-dog bun, chili-topped); Chicago dog
w: Cash-only Marquette Park trailer open since 1972 that 'looks like a strong wind might blow it over' — on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.

dish: Rib tips and hot links from the aquarium smoker, with sauce and fries
w: Founded 1954 by the Lemons brothers and still family-run; South Side aquarium-smoker rib tips. 2025 James Beard America's Classics award.

dish: Hong Kong-style BBQ; the Peking duck three-course feast
w: Uptown Hong Kong barbecue house near Argyle, family-run since 1987; 2018 James Beard America's Classics award.

dish: Wiener schnitzel, sauerbraten, house root beer at the old bar
w: German restaurant and bar in the Loop since 1898 — its bar held Chicago's first post-Prohibition liquor license. A James Beard America's Classics honoree.

dish: House-smoked shrimp, salmon and chubs; fried perch and smelt
w: Smokehouse shack by the 95th Street bridge on the Calumet River since 1948, wood-smoking fish on site. A James Beard America's Classics honoree.

dish: The original Maxwell Street Polish with grilled onions and mustard; the bone-in pork chop sandwich
w: Open around the clock since 1939 — the stand that claims the original Maxwell Street Polish. Time Out calls it the best Polish in the city; its pork chop sandwich is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.

dish: The jibarito — steak pressed between fried green plantains with garlic mayo
w: 'Home of the Jibarito': Juan 'Peter' Figueroa's Humboldt Park restaurant created the plantain sandwich in 1996. Tops the Infatuation's jibarito guide and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.

dish: Baby back ribs with the zesty sauce; chili
w: Old Town rib tavern open since 1932 (a Sinatra hangout), neon beer signs intact — on the Infatuation's old-school list and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats for its baby backs.

dish: Hot fudge sundae in a clamshell dish with house hot fudge
w: Ice-cream parlor and candy shop at Armitage & Western since 1921 — the Infatuation's old-school list and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats (hot fudge sundae).

dish: Bone-in rib eye; chicken alla Joe
w: River North steakhouse in its wood-frame building since 1941 — as old-school as Chicago gets (Infatuation), rib eye on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.

dish: Corned beef sandwich, potato latkes, matzo ball soup, cafeteria-style
w: South Loop cafeteria deli since 1942, lunchroom of generations of politicians — reviewed by the Infatuation ('still great after 80 years') and on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats for its corned beef.

dish: Goat birria tatemada with handmade tortillas and consomé
w: Family-run Archer Heights birrieria devoted to Jalisco-style roasted goat. Michelin Bib Gourmand; birria on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.

address: 430 N Michigan Ave (lower level), Chicago, IL 60611
w: Lower Michigan Avenue newspapermen's tavern since 1934 — 'cheezborger, cheezborger, no Pepsi, Coke' of SNL fame and the Cubs' goat curse.
dish: The double cheezborger

w: Deep-dish institution since 1966 near the Mag Mile, its cornmeal-crust pies served in graffiti-covered booths diners are invited to sign.
dish: Cornmeal-crust deep dish with a sausage patty

w: The River North beef stand (since 1979) that inspired The Bear's Original Beef of Chicagoland — dipped beef with hot giardiniera.
dish: Italian beef, dipped, with hot giardiniera
The Rainbow Cone — chocolate, strawberry, Palmer House (cherry-walnut), pistachio and orange sherbet, sliced not scooped
w: Beverly's pink stand serving its five-flavour sliced cone since 1926 — a South Side institution (Choose Chicago) and one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Stephanie Izard's Randolph Street flagship (2010) that made the West Loop a dining district — the pig-face plate is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
dish: Wood-oven pig face with a sunny egg; goat empanadas

w: Paul Kahan's cedar-lined Mediterranean wine bar (2003) — its chorizo-stuffed, bacon-wrapped dates are one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
dish: Chorizo-stuffed, bacon-wrapped Medjool dates; focaccia

w: Greektown's taverna since 1971 — flaming saganaki ('Opa!') is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
dish: Flaming saganaki ('Opa!'), lamb, grilled octopus

w: Skokie deli opened in the 1960s as a hub for Holocaust survivors — one of Chicagoland's oldest Jewish delis; bagel and lox on Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
dish: Bagel and lox; corned beef

w: Lincoln Park's late-night char-dog stand (to 4am weekends), as famous for the staff's good-natured verbal abuse as for its dogs.
dish: Char dog with everything; cheddar fries

w: Humboldt Park bakery run by the same family since 1911 — custom cakes, strudel, coffee cake and paczki.
dish: Strudel, coffee cake, custom cakes, Fat Tuesday paczki

w: The traders' bar in the Board of Trade lobby, notorious for a 'jack and coke' that's a giant cup of whiskey with the can on the side.
dish: The oversized 'jack and coke'; diner breakfasts

w: The taproom attached to Goose Island's production brewery (brewing here since 1995) — test batches and Bourbon County Stout rarities.
dish: Bourbon County Stout, Sofie, test batches
